content.title: Invasive strategy in NSTE-ACS
content.summary: Guidance on when to use invasive coronary strategy in patients with non-ST-elevation acute coronary syndromes (NSTE-ACS), including immediate, early (within 24 h), selective, and routine invasive approaches based on risk strata.

recommendations.recommendation: An invasive strategy during hospital admission is recommended in NSTE-ACS patients with high-risk criteria or a high index of suspicion for unstable angina.
recommendations.notes: Applies to patients meeting high-risk criteria or high clinical suspicion of unstable angina.

recommendations.recommendation: A selective invasive approach is recommended in patients without very high- or high-risk NSTE-ACS criteria and with a low index of suspicion for NSTE-ACS.
recommendations.notes: Approach for lower-risk patients where immediate invasive management is not indicated.

recommendations.recommendation: An immediate invasive strategy is recommended in patients with a working diagnosis of NSTE-ACS and with at least one of the following very high-risk criteria.
very_high_risk_criteria: Recurrent or refractory chest pain despite medical treatment
Acute heart failure presumed secondary to ongoing myocardial ischaemia
Recurrent dynamic ST-segment or T wave changes, particularly intermittent ST-segment elevation
recommendations.notes: Immediate invasive strategy indicated when any listed very-high-risk feature is present.

recommendations.recommendation: An early invasive strategy within 24 h should be considered in patients with at least one of the following high-risk criteria.
high_risk_criteria: Confirmed diagnosis of NSTEMI based on current recommended ESC high-sensitivity cardiac troponin (hs-cTn) algorithms
Dynamic ST-segment or T wave changes
recommendations.notes: Early invasive (<24 h) recommended for patients with listed high-risk features.

abbreviations_and_notes.GRACE: Global Registry of Acute Coronary Events
abbreviations_and_notes.hs-cTn: high-sensitivity cardiac troponin (biomarker; not presented as a gene on this page)

content.references_note: Reference citations listed on the page (e.g., 196–200, 202, 226–230) support the recommendations.
content.footnotes: ST-segment elevation equivalents are presented in supplementary data (figure referenced on page).
